jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff Engineering
jobs.description:
Overview

Physical Superintelligence is a startup with roots at Google, NVIDIA, Harvard, Meta, MIT, Oxford, Johns Hopkins, Cambridge, and the Perimeter Institute building AI systems to discover new physics at scale. We are seeking engineers to build platform infrastructure at the intersection of computational science, AI systems, and software engineering.

Our mission is to discover and commercialize transformative physics breakthroughs at scale with artificial superintelligence, safely, verifiably, and for broad public benefit.

The last century's golden age of physics gave us transistors, lasers, and nuclear energy. We believe artificial superintelligence will unlock the next one. We're creating the infrastructure to industrialize scientific discovery and usher in this new era.

We have one product: new physics, at scale.

Use this application if you are an engineer, no open engineering role fits your profile, and you want to be considered anyway. We hire excellent engineers when we find them, whether or not a matching role is open. Tell us how your background and ambitions intersect with our mission, and where you would have the most impact.

Â 

Role and Responsibilities

  • Our platform spans distributed systems, data infrastructure, agent systems and evaluation, HPC and scientific computing, developer platforms, product engineering, cloud infrastructure, and security. This application is for engineers who are strong across most of that list, or unusually deep in something important we did not list. The bar here is higher than any single posting.

  • The standard is the same as every engineering role here: full ownership from spec to ship to on-call, and systems other people build on.

  • Be specific about where you would have the most impact and what you would work on first.

  • We review these applications on a rolling basis and respond only when we see a strong fit.

What We're Looking For

  • A track record of shipping substantive engineering work: systems that shipped and mattered, open source people depend on, infrastructure that outlived your tenure. We weight evidence over credentials.

  • Depth in several of the areas above and the range to move between them, or singular depth in something important we did not list.

  • You can walk us through a hard technical decision you made, what you traded away, and what you would do differently.

  • A concrete reason to be here. If AI systems and physical science together is why you are applying, say so specifically.

Nice to Have

  • Background in any of our named areas: distributed systems, data infrastructure, agent systems and evals, HPC and scientific computing, developer platforms, product engineering, infrastructure, or security.

  • Experience in research or scientific computing environments.

  • Something we can read or run: a design doc, a paper, a repo, a postmortem.

Â 

How We Work

We hold a high technical bar and give people full ownership of their work, from spec to ship to on-call. We write contracts before logic, test against real systems instead of mocks, and favor simple designs that ship over clever ones that do not. Our development process is AI-native: we work with agentic coding tools daily, write specs that are legible to humans and agents alike, and lead with leverage.

Â 

Location and Compensation

This role is based in Boston. We will consider remote candidates on a case-by-case basis. We offer competitive compensation including salary, benefits, and meaningful early-stage equity. We evaluate on technical breadth, systems thinking, scientific curiosity, and shipping velocity. We are an equal opportunity employer and value diverse perspectives in building platforms for AI-driven discovery.

jobs.description:
About Pivotal Health

Pivotal Health is the leading technology platform that helps healthcare providers get paid fairly in an increasingly complex reimbursement landscape.

Today, many providers face persistent underpayment from health insurance companies, despite delivering high-quality care. While processes like IDR (Independent Dispute Resolution) were designed to promote fairness, theyâre often administrative-heavy, time-consuming, and difficult to navigate without the right tools.

Pivotal Health combines software, data, and service into a seamlessly integrated, AI-driven platform that simplifies these complex reimbursement workflows. We help providers efficiently dispute underpaid claims, reduce administrative burden, and recover the reimbursement theyâre entitled to; without adding more work to already stretched teams.

Our full-service IDR solution is just the starting point. Weâre building solutions that enable providers to operate with clarity, control, and confidence across the reimbursement journey.

About the Role

We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join Pivotal's Case Execution team. This team owns critical parts of the case execution workflow, including eligibility, batching, submissions, ops workflows, and claim orchestration. These systems sit at the operational core of how Pivotal delivers outcomes for providers.

This is a strong fit for an engineer who enjoys solving complex, workflow-driven backend problems and working through data-heavy decision logic. The most technically demanding areas for this team are eligibility and batching, and the right person is energized by that kind of work rather than looking to avoid it.

What You'll Do

  • Build and improve core case execution systems: Own backend development across eligibility, batching, submissions, ops workflows, and claim orchestration. These are the systems that determine how cases move through Pivotal's platform and reach resolution.

  • Tackle complex, data-driven backend problems: Work through the decision logic and data-heavy workflows that make eligibility and batching hard, understanding not just how individual systems work, but how they interact across the broader platform.

Who You Are

  • Strong engineering fundamentals with hands-on experience building data-heavy, workflow-oriented systems

  • Experience working on complex, data-driven decision logic or orchestration problems: you're comfortable with systems where correctness and sequencing both matter

  • Comfortable operating in a collaborative, fast-moving startup environment where ownership and requirements evolve

  • Python experience; able to work effectively in a Python-based backend environment

  • Self-directed and proactive: you identify problems and drive them to resolution without heavy oversight

  • Strong communicator who collaborates well across engineering, product, and adjacent teams

Extra Credit If You Have

  • Some front-end experience to support admin workflow contributions

Why Youâll Love Working Here

While we primarily hire around our core hubsâLos Angeles and New Yorkâwe remain open to exceptional talent outside those regions. Remote and hybrid flexibility varies by role and team, and is outlined in each job description.

If youâre excited by solving complex problems and making a real-world impact, weâd love to hear from you.

Benefits Include:

  • Full health, dental, and vision coverage

  • Retirement savings plan through 401(k)

  • Flexible time off

  • Opportunities for company-wide connection and events

Ready to Make an Impact?
Weâre building something meaningful; and we want you on the team.

Bring your ideas, curiosity, and drive, and letâs transform healthcare reimbursement together.

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Brand Protection & Marketplace Compliance Analyst
jobs.description:
Position Type: Full-time

Location: Philippines (Remote)

Schedule: Mon-Fri, EST

About the Company

Our client is a global leader in swimming pool technology, specializing in robotic pool cleaners, pool safety products, water treatment solutions, and related pool equipment for residential and commercial customers. With a strong international presence and a network of distributors, subsidiaries, and partners across multiple markets, our client serves customers worldwide through a variety of sales and distribution channels.

About the Role

Our client is looking for a Brand Protection & Marketplace Compliance Analyst to monitor online marketplaces and digital channels across North America and Europe. The role focuses on identifying unauthorized sellers, marketplace and distribution violations, misuse of brand assets, and other compliance issues.

You will conduct online research, analyze seller and product data, maintain accurate records, and prepare reports that provide actionable insights to the business.

Responsibilities

  • Identify MAP, distribution, territory, and marketplace compliance issues.

  • Monitor unauthorized use of logos, images, trademarks, and product content.

  • Collect evidence such as URLs, screenshots, seller information, and product details.

  • Maintain accurate seller databases and internal records.

  • Prepare daily reports and monthly Voice of Consumer reports.

  • Build and maintain dashboards tracking brand-protection metrics.

  • Identify opportunities to improve research and reporting processes.

Competencies and Qualifications


Must-Have

  • 3+ years of experience in data analysis, online research, e-commerce, compliance, or a related field.

  • Strong Excel skills, including pivot tables.

  • Strong research, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

  • Excellent attention to detail and data accuracy.

  • Strong written English and reporting skills.

  • Familiarity with Amazon and other e-commerce marketplaces.

Nice-to-Have

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

As Alan’s Corporate Paralegal, you will own the corporate governance of a fast-growing international group (six jurisdictions and a dozen entities today, more in the coming months) and rebuild how that work gets done with AI. The role has three parts:

Automate the repetitive work with AI.

  • Improved our templates and documentation;

  • Reviewed or drafted legal documents in several areas;

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

⭐ The Product Marketing Manager B2C opportunity

Building the engagement engine with Alan Play that makes 500k members come back to their health every single day, a key differentiator for Alan.

 

Today, 25k Alan members open Alan Play every day (120,000 every month) to walk, meditate, breathe, compete with their colleagues, build healthy habits. Play is Alan's #1 source of traffic and the retention engine of all our health services. And we are B2B2C: companies pay, members choose to engage. Play is a differentiator in deals, and at renewal. HR admins are also an underused distribution channel to reach members. Two audiences, one product story. By 2030 we want 500k daily users, across all our countries

 

The challenges: Our lifecycle is greenfield. Onboarding, activation, reminders, reactivation and win-back are owned by nobody today. We run events rebuilt almost from scratch, so the tenth Alan Cup costs as much as the first. We measure opens and clicks, not what a campaign actually did to daily engagement. And on the B2B side, our pitch goes stale between releases, as Play ships fast, so the sales argument does not keep up.

 

The future: A lifecycle layer designed for personalisation, running on the segmentation and experimentation platform Play has been building. Campaign machinery that gets cheaper every quarter. A measurement loop we trust, with holdouts and real incrementality. A live Play pitch that updates as features ship, so the field walks into a renewal or a deal with the current product. And HR admins turned into a real, measured distribution channel rather than a mailing list.

 

The hard parts: This role is horizontal, and vertical. Many member segments, many admin segments, several countries, coordination with Product as well as Sales, KAM and CSM, as well as other products teams who communicate with members.

 

⭐ Is it you we’re looking for?

 

Must haves

  • Retention and lifecycle marketing at scale on a consumer product - subscription, gaming, social, media, health and fitness. Where engagement and retention are the business.

  • You build systems, not just campaigns - you can walk us through machinery you built that made the next campaign cheaper, and tell us what it cost you to get it adopted.

  • Analytical rigour - you read a funnel, design a segment, set up a holdout, call a result. You are comfortable being accountable to a product metric.

  • Horizontal operator - you have held many audiences and several countries at once. Volume and context switching, not depth on a single vertical.

  • Genuinely hands on - you want to run the campaigns yourself at the start. This is the ramp up, and the condition for standardising well afterwards.

  • Branding sensitivity : you can express the personality of the product you market and create great moments

  • You write well and fast. Emotion generating copy and branding is a real part of the job

  • Marketing automation at scale - Customer.io, Braze, Iterable or equivalent.

  • Missionary mindset and a real attachment to the health mission.

  • B2B2C sensibility: you can maintain weigh in both segments

 

Nice to haves

  • French, Spanish or Dutch on top of English, for four-country localisation

  • HR tech, employee benefits or workplace wellbeing

  • Gamification, challenges or social mechanics

  • Experience standardising something that other teams then reused

 

Not a fit if

  • You describe success in open and click rates

  • You only want to talk to members, and see commercial side as somebody else's job

  • You need a brief, or someone who writes the strategy for you

  • You want to delegate execution from day one

  • You treat positioning as PMM-only territory, or platform teams as a service desk

  • You are uncomfortable with ambiguity, or need a big team to be effective

     

🙌 Perks & Benefits


At Alan, we believe that being in good health is a basic need, and it starts with our employees. This is why Alaners are provided with a stimulating environment and perks ensuring they are happy, efficient and spend only high-quality time with co-workers.

Therefore, we offer:

  • Flexible Office. Amazing office space at our HQ, sponsored co-working hubs or a full-remote experience with home office equipment sponsorship, we want you to live where you’re the happiest.

  • All the tools you need. Top of the range equipment: Macbook Pro, keyboard, laptop stand, monitor, and Bose noise-canceling headphones.

  • Flexible vacation policy and flexible working hours. Organize your time as you wish.

  • Transport. Country-specific commuter benefits.

  • Learning & Training opportunities. A highly flexible Training policy free books and budget to attend and speak at conferences if the opportunity arises.

  • Personal growth through coaching: At Alan, coaching isn't just a perk - it's core to who we are. Every Alaner is paired with a dedicated coach from day one, who helps maximize their impact, nurture engagement, and navigate Alan's values to develop their full potential. Learn more about our coaching culture.

 

Important note: we hire people, not roles.

If you're excited about this opportunity but don't check every box, we'd love to hear from you. Everyone, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply as it can only bring learnings or success.

If you identify yourself as a woman: Did you know that research shows women often apply only when meeting 100% of requirements?

We'll be thrilled to receive your application!

Alan is looking for a Global Brand Event Manager to turn events into a distinctive, scalable expression of the Alan brand. The role combines event strategy, brand experience, operational excellence, commercial understanding, and community building.

You will own Alan’s yearly flagship event, building on the success of Alan 10, and help make it an even stronger moment for brand, community, customers, prospects, partners, and the wider healthcare ecosystem. Beyond the flagship event, you will build the operating system that enables commercial and local teams to run high-quality events repeatedly and consistently.

It is a senior individual-contributor role that owns the global event system and makes other teams more autonomous and effective.

You will lead the global strategy and execution of Alan’s major Brand events, while owning the execution of local Brand events in France. You will create the playbooks, standards, templates, and measurement frameworks that allow teams across markets to deliver high-quality events without reinventing the wheel each time.

You will also contribute to the Brand team’s global community-event strategy, identifying the formats and moments that can make Alan more visible, credible, and memorable to the communities we want to influence.

You’ll equip local teams with the right local approach and assets, and support them as they adapt and run events in their markets.

Main responsibilities

  1. Own Alan’s yearly flagship event

    • Participate in the definition of the event’s purpose, audience, positioning, narrative, and success criteria.

    • Build the event roadmap, budget, and production plan.

    • Manage agencies, venues, suppliers, speakers, partners, and internal stakeholders.

    • Coordinate content, creative, production, guest management, press, influencers, Sales, and local market teams.

    • Design a high-quality guest experience before, during, and after the event.

    • Connect invitations, registration, CRM tracking, attendance, and follow-up.

    • Run rehearsals, speaker preparation, run-of-show management, and on-site execution.

  2. Build Alan’s recurring event playbook

    • Define the main event formats and their intended purposes, such as owned events, executive dinners, round tables, speaking opportunities, trade shows, and partner events.

    • Create practical templates for briefs, timelines, budgets, approvals, execution, production, and follow-up.

    • Help define the role of commercial teams before, during, and after the event.

    • Create reusable content, event assets, checklists, and quality standards.

  3. Support local teams on local events

    • Help local teams choose the right format and define the desired outcome.

    • Review briefs and plans, provide feedback, and raise the quality bar.

    • Identify successful local formats that could be scaled globally.

  4. Help shape and execute Alan’s community-event strategy

    • Contribute with the Brand team to the Community building strategy

    • Design recurring event franchises and formats.

    • Build partnerships with relevant organizations, experts, customers, and opinion leaders.

    • Run test-and-learn initiatives that can start locally and scale globally.

Profile & Competencies

We are looking for someone who has:

  • At least 5 years of experience delivering events end to end, ideally in a Brand, B2B marketing or agency environment.

  • A track record of creating original event concepts and formats, not only executing a brief.

  • Strong editorial judgement: the right angle, speakers and content to make an event memorable.

  • Brand creativity: a clear point of view on how an event expresses a brand.

  • Experience running complex events with multiple stakeholders, agencies, suppliers and speakers (including profiles with special logistics and security needs).

  • Strong production skills: planning, budgeting, vendor and risk management, rehearsals and on-site delivery.

  • Experience building repeatable processes, playbooks or templates.

  • A strong understanding of how events drive brand, community and commercial outcomes, and comfort with CRM, registration, lead capture and follow-up.

  • Experience working with Sales, Marketing, PR, Creative and local market teams.

  • Fluent in French

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.

  • Based in (or willing to relocate to) Paris, and willing to travel across international markets.

🚀 The Challenge

  • Alan is a leading European health insurer with over 1 million members across 4 countries (France, Belgium, Spain, Canada). At its core, Alan is a tech company that believes exceptional member experience is a competitive advantage: fast, empathetic, and reliable service at scale. As of Q1 2026, 40% of conversations are handled automatically.

  • At the intersection of Care, Legal, Security, and Data Protection sits a set of topics that are as operationally complex as they are strategically critical: data breaches, GDPR rights requests, security incidents, legal complaints, regulatory reporting.

  • We are looking for a Care Legal & Security Specialist to own these topics end-to-end: handling complex cases in close collaboration with Alan's Legal and DPO teams, building the processes and training that allow our ~300 Care agents to manage them with confidence, and identifying where AI and automation can reduce manual load. As Alan accelerates across four countries, what you build in France gets replicated in Spain, Belgium, and Canada: your work doesn't stay local.

  • This is not a pure legal role, and it is not a pure ops role. You handle regulatory cases, improve the processes that prevent them from recurring, and scale what works across countries. You will be embedded within our Operational Excellence team, working in close collaboration with Care Ops and the Corporate Unit.

    👨‍🚀 Missions

    1/ Operational run (60%)

  • Handle complex security incidents, GDPR cases, and legal complaints escalated from Care agents, including CNIL notifications (drafted in close collaboration with Legal and DPO, within the 72-hour regulatory deadline), account takeover situations, Level 2 and Level 3 complaints, and incoming legal mail

  • Manage interactions with external stakeholders (CNIL, Insurance Ombudsman, Signal Conso) with precision and within regulatory deadlines

  • Own KPI monitoring and reporting for legal and security matters; organize yearly complaints reporting for Alan's Board; identify trends and escalate systemic issues to Product teams early

    2/ Scalability: process, tools, and training (20%)

  • Design and continuously improve workflows, escalation paths, macros, and help center content so Care agents can handle legal and security cases autonomously at L1 and L2

  • Identify simplification and automation opportunities across legal and security operations, then collaborate with Care Ops and Product crews to deploy them, rather than solving each case manually

  • Build and maintain training materials (case studies, Q&As, simulations), so Care Experts develop real judgment, not just process familiarity

  • Ensure regulatory training completion across the team

    3/ Globalization (20%)

  • Translate processes, frameworks, and training materials built for France into resources that Care and Legal/Compliance teams in other countries can adopt

  • Coordinate actively with counterparts in other countries to share learnings, align on best practices, and anticipate regulatory divergences

  • Build shared resources so that when a new country goes live, the Care Legal & Security function isn't starting from scratch

To deliver on those missions, you will:

  • Support Care Experts participating in the Legal & Security taskforce: build their judgment on complex and ambiguous cases, be the primary escalation reference for Care agents facing difficult legal or security situations

  • Collaborate with the Corporate Unit Lead and Care Ops to shape the Care roadmap on legal and security topics; translate regulatory constraints into executable processes and surface operational insights that should inform policy or product decisions

    ⭐ You'll excel in this role if you:

  • Deliver reliably on high-stakes, deadline-driven cases with a real member-centric mindset

  • Have at least 1-2 years of experience in one of the following: GDPR / privacy operations, legal complaints handling in a regulated sector, or compliance ops in fintech, insurtech, or health

  • Communicate with precision and adapt to your audience, whether you're briefing a legal expert, aligning with a product team, or coaching a front-line agent. You get buy-in from agents and managers who didn't ask for a new process, and that's as important as designing the process itself

  • Spot simplification opportunities and know how to turn them into projects: you identify what should be automated or redesigned, then drive the collaboration with Care Ops and Product to make it happen

  • Are comfortable navigating regulatory frameworks (GDPR, complaint handling, CNIL) without being a lawyer; you know when to escalate and when to own it, and you're backed by Legal and DPO experts at Alan

  • Are comfortable making judgment calls in ambiguous situations and moving forward without waiting for all the answers.

  • Are fluent in French (C1+ written and spoken, essential for CNIL notifications, ombudsman responses, and legal correspondence) and proficient in English for internal Alan collaboration

    No prior legal qualification is required but a background in law is a genuine plus. We are looking for operational rigor, strong communication, and the appetite to build something that scales.

For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the B-C level range.

MoonPay is for builders with something to prove.

This isn't a "work on cool crypto stuff" company. It's a high-standards, high-velocity, high-accountability company building the operating system for value movement. If the internet moves information, we move value: crypto, stablecoins, tokenized assets, and whatever comes next. Four offerings make that real: fund, tokenize, trade, and spend. 30M+ customers and 500+ ecosystem partners run on us. Licensed in the U.S. Regulated across the UK, EU, Canada, and Australia.

AI is the default operating mode here. It's woven into every role, and we expect you to use it daily. It handles the manual work so you can deliver on what actually matters.

You'll thrive here if outcomes excite you more than process, if impact motivates you more than titles, and if you want hard problems, real ownership, and teammates who love winning, building, and doing it together.

The bar is high. The pace is real. We're building for what's next, for humans and agents.

Recent recognition:


Forbes' America's Best Startup Employers 2026 .
2nd in Crypto Services on Fortune's inaugural Crypto 100
The Sunday Times Best Places to Work two years running

Research has shown that women are less likely than men to apply for this role if they do not have experience in 100% of these areas. Please know that this list is indicative, and that we would still love to hear from you even if you feel that you are only a 75% match. Skills can be learned, diversity cannot.


About the Opportunity

In this role, you will join MoonPay’s Crypto Asset Management team as a Product Manager, helping us build and scale the liquidity and asset infrastructure that supports products across MoonPay.

The team is responsible for how liquidity is sourced and distributed across our platform, supporting high-value crypto transaction volumes across multiple assets, venues, and blockchains. As our remit expands across products including Ramps, Swaps, and Enterprise, the volume and complexity of product work is growing with it.

You will take ownership of day-to-day product execution across our on-chain and off-chain workstreams, helping turn business and technical requirements into clearly defined, prioritised, and executable work.

Working closely with the Principal Product Manager, Engineering, Operations, Compliance, Finance, Treasury, and commercial teams, you will support initiatives including liquidity-provider integrations, asset availability, routing and best-execution capabilities, custody and wallet infrastructure, and the broader on-chain services required to operate reliably at scale.

Your work will help the team move faster, improve the efficiency and resilience of our liquidity infrastructure, and enable MoonPay to support significantly more products and transaction volume as the business grows.

This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys solving complex problems, wants to deepen their understanding of crypto and financial infrastructure, and is excited to develop their product craft in a fast-moving, high-impact environment.

What You Will Do

  • Own day-to-day product execution across Crypto Asset Management initiatives, translating business, technical, operational, and compliance requirements into clear product requirements, user stories, project plans, and delivery milestones.

  • Support integrations with new liquidity sources, including centralised exchanges, OTC trading desks, and decentralised services, helping expand MoonPay’s liquidity network and improve sourcing efficiency, reliability, and execution.

Join a squad dedicated to revolutionizing how legal professionals advise clients and businesses across France and Europe. A high-impact product squad responsible for secondary legal sources and private documents. These are complex challenges where you will also contribute to embedding GenAI at the core of our products. 

You can find full details about our stack on GitHub https://github.com/DoctrineLegal/#our-tech-stack !
 
Note: Previous professional experience in law is not required, but a willingness to learn and develop expertise in understanding legal documents is important 🙂

  • Develop NLP models (whether based on Machine Learning or not) to assist with information search and recommendation within legal documents, in particular.

  • Collaborate with different types of profiles, including engineers, product managers, and product designers, to identify new product development opportunities.
  • Participate in internal knowledge sharing and consolidation of best practices; contribute to the development of our Engineering strategy.

    • Ideal Profile 👀
  • Strong knowledge of Machine Learning (both classical and deep learning) for data extraction and recommendation, ideally with some first-hand experience with LLMs.
  • Experience with natural language search engines and inverted indexes such as Elasticsearch.
  • Solid understanding of MLOps challenges, with a strong motivation to grow in this area.
  • A keen interest in artificial intelligence topics.
  • Desire to identify, analyze, and deploy the latest scientific advances in production.
  • Strong Python development skills, with a focus on algorithm design.
  • Proficiency in French, as you will be working with legal data in French.

    🌱 Real internal mobility opportunities

    🏄‍♂️ Regular team events

    🏋️‍♀️ A Gymlib subscription for sports and wellness activities

    🧘 Free access to the Moka.care mental health support platform, including up to 6 individual sessions per year

    👩‍⚕️ Health insurance with Alan

    🍱🚲 A Swile card for meal vouchers and sustainable mobility allowance (€66.60/month)

    💡 Discounts and perks via our Works Council (CSE) on the Happypal platform

    🍏 Brand new Apple equipment

    Our values 🤝

    At Doctrine, our 4 values guide us every day as we work to move things forward.

    Challenge the status quo: we champion bold ideas that drive change across an entire industry.

    Liberty and responsibility: we encourage autonomy, individual impact and ownership.

    Knowledge is power: information is at the heart of Doctrine's mission, and we constantly strive to grow.

    Release early, release often and listen to your customers: we believe in the power of iteration and in constantly listening to our market, our customers and their challenges.

    1. A 30-min intro call with one of our Talent Acquisition Managers to understand your career goals and walk you through what we're building at Doctrine.

Notre ambition ? Permettre aux professionnels du droit de gagner en fiabilité, en efficacité et en sérénité, grâce à une plateforme unique, exhaustive et sécurisée.

jobs.title: Stage IA/ML Engineer 100% R&D - agentic AI
jobs.description:
INTERNSHIP 

Agentic AI for Semi-Automating the Data Science Workflow 

Ekimetrics is the European leader in data science, with over 500 data scientists and 1,000+ projects since 2006. With offices in Paris, London, New York, and Hong Kong, we conduct projects in over 50 countries across various sectors, including financial services, retail, telecom, healthcare, and more. 

Our mission is to help companies audit their data opportunities, enhance their analytical capital, and deploy actionable solutions that maximize their marketing and operational performance while reinvigorating business models. 

Our absolute focus is on delivering short-term gains while ensuring the long-term development of our clients' data capital. We are committed to offering the most advanced data science approaches and building ethical, sustainable AI practices. 

Key Figures 

  • 20 years of experience in data science 

  • 500+ data scientists, all consultants 

  • 5 offices in Paris, London, New York, Hong Kong, and Shanghai 

  • 350+ clients (CAC40, Fortune500) 

  • $1M+ in profit generated for our clients since 2006 

  • 1,000+ data science projects 

Within Ekimetrics, the Innovation Department works on AI research topics in collaboration with our industrial and academic partners. The department comprises several PhD experts in generative AI, deep learning, computer vision, time series, explainability, and causality. Each expert leads teams tasked with studying and building state-of-the-art methods and adapting them to specific business problems, developing new methodologies or algorithms to address identified challenges, and ensuring a seamless handover for integration within Ekimetrics' industrial ecosystem. 

A central focus of the Innovation Department is closing the gap between cutting-edge AI agents and the day-to-day reality of delivering data science at scale. The department is investing in agentic systems that accelerate the data science lifecycle while keeping data scientists firmly in control of quality, governance, and business relevance. This internship sits at the heart of that effort, combining applied AI research with production-grade engineering on Ekimetrics' modern data stack. 

Internship Objective: From a Business Question to a Trusted Recommendation 

LLM-based agents have made rapid progress in the past two years: they can now write, run and tune machine learning code with little human help. Yet real data science projects rarely start from a clean, well-defined task. They start from a business question and imperfect data, and the early choices (what to predict, how to measure success, how to validate) decide whether the result can be trusted. Automating these steps calls for assistants that know when to ask, when to stop, and how to back every claim with evidence. 

The Innovation Department is building remit, a harness that semi-automates the data science workflow. At each step of a project (framing, data design, exploratory analysis, modeling, evaluation), AI agents draft the output, automatic checks catch common mistakes such as data leakage, and a data scientist reviews and accepts the result before moving on. Ultimately, a business user brings a question and a dataset, and the system frames the problem, prepares and explores the data, compares models against a simple baseline, and returns a clear recommendation in which every figure can be traced back to the data. 

The work builds on recent research in agentic data science [1]. Agents now earn medals on many of the Kaggle competitions in MLE-bench [2], yet they tend to guess silently rather than ask when a task is ambiguous [3]. Meanwhile, tabular foundation models such as TabICLv2 [4] give strong predictive models without any tuning. 

The intern will work with senior data scientists and AI builders to build and refine remit. This internship offers an opportunity to engage with cutting-edge AI research and production engineering. 

Key Responsibilities 

The intern will: 

  • Review the latest research on agentic data science and on the evaluation of AI agents, building on the team's recent review. 

  • Design and implement remit's agents, starting with problem framing and data design, together with the automatic checks that catch mistakes such as data leakage. 

  • Help define how the system works with business users: when to ask a clarifying question, when to stop rather than guess, and how to explain results in plain language. 

  • Extend the system toward modeling and evaluation, building on trusted tools (scikit-learn, AutoML, tabular foundation models) rather than free-form generated code. 

  • Build a benchmark of realistic business cases, run experiments to measure quality, reliability and cost, and take part in a pilot with business users. 

  • Help integrate the system with the Databricks stack (Unity Catalog, MLflow) and support the safe and governed operation of the agents. 

Profile 

  • Currently in the final year of a Master's or Engineering degree, with strong foundations in machine learning, statistics, and programming. 

  • Good grasp of model validation: train/test splits, data leakage, baselines. 

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work autonomously on an open-ended research-and-build problem and to explain results to non-specialists. 

  • Familiarity with large language models and agentic techniques (prompting, tool calling, structured outputs, evaluation). 

  • Strong Python skills and a solid command of the standard data science toolkit (pandas/polars, scikit-learn, gradient-boosting libraries). 

  • Fluency in English. 

  • Nice to have: experience with an agent framework, solid software engineering practices (git, code review, testing), and exposure to Databricks, MLflow or cloud data platforms. 

Benefits 

  • Hands-on Research & Engineering Experience: Build a pioneering agentic system on real data science workflows, contributing to a tool with direct real-world impact. 

  • Collaborative Learning: Engage with a team of data scientists, AI experts, and PhDs in a dynamic, research-driven environment within Ekimetrics' Innovation Department. 

  • Skill Development: Gain expertise in LLM agents, the evaluation of AI systems, and production tooling on Databricks (Unity Catalog, MLflow). 

  • Career Growth: Opportunity to transition into a full-time Data Scientist role in AI at Ekimetrics, or into a PhD program, upon successful completion of the internship. 

  • Scientific Contribution: Opportunity to co-author and publish scientific papers in reputable AI and data science conferences and journals. 

  • Networking: Collaborate with Ekimetrics' industrial and academic partners, enhancing your professional network in the AI research community. 

  • Ethical and Sustainable AI: Learn to develop AI solutions that align with ethical, governed, and sustainable best practices, a core commitment of Ekimetrics. 

Duration: 6 months, Paris 

References 

[1] LLM-Based Data Science Agents: A Survey of Capabilities, Challenges, and Future Directions (2025). https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04023 

[2] MLE-bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Machine Learning Engineering (2025). https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07095 

[3] Ambig-DS: A Benchmark for Task-Framing Ambiguity in Data-Science Agents (2026). https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09698 

[4] TabICLv2: A Better, Faster, Scalable, and Open Tabular Foundation Model (2026). https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11139

jobs.title: Stage 2027 AI/ML Engineer 100% R&D - Tabular foundation models
jobs.description:
Latent Reasoning for Tabular Foundation Models: Performance Enhancement and Interpretability 

 

 

Ekimetrics is the European leader in data science, with over 500 data scientists and 1,000+ projects since 2006. With offices in Paris, London, New York, and Hong Kong, we conduct projects in over 50 countries across various sectors, including financial services, retail, telecom, healthcare, and more. 

Our mission is to help companies audit their data opportunities, enhance their analytical capital, and deploy actionable solutions that maximize their marketing and operational performance while reinvigorating business models. 

Our absolute focus is on delivering short-term gains while ensuring the long-term development of our clients' data capital. We are committed to offering the most advanced data science approaches and building ethical, sustainable AI practices. 

Key Figures 

  • 20 years of experience in data science 

  • 500+ data scientists, all consultants 

  • 5 offices in Paris, London, New York, Hong Kong, and Shanghai 

  • 350+ clients (CAC40, Fortune500) 

  • $1M+ in profit generated for our clients since 2006 

  • 1,000+ data science projects 

Within Ekimetrics, the Innovation Department works on AI research topics in collaboration with our industrial and academic partners. The department comprises several PhD experts in generative AI, deep learning, computer vision, time series, explainability, and causality. Each expert leads teams tasked with studying and building state-of-the-art methods and adapting them to specific business problems, developing new methodologies or algorithms to address identified challenges, and ensuring a seamless handover for integration within Ekimetrics' industrial ecosystem. 

A central focus of the Innovation Department is closing the gap between cutting-edge AI agents and the day-to-day reality of delivering data science at scale. The department is investing in agentic systems that accelerate the data science lifecycle while keeping data scientists firmly in control of quality, governance, and business relevance. This internship sits at the heart of that effort, combining applied AI research with production-grade engineering on Ekimetrics' modern data stack. 

 

Internship Objective: From Latent Reasoning to Better and More Understandable Tabular Models 

 

Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) such as TabPFN, TabICL or TabDPT are transformers pre-trained on large collections of mostly synthetic datasets. They learn in context: the training data and the points to predict are given as input, and predictions come out of a single forward pass, with no dataset-specific training or tuning. They now rival gradient boosting on many benchmarks [3], which is changing how tabular modeling is practiced. 

In large language models, a growing line of research lets the model “reason” in its latent space rather than through generated tokens, using extra depth-wise computation, reused continuous hidden states or internal iterations. This latent reasoning can improve performance without longer text outputs [1, 2]. Our hypothesis is that a similar mechanism can improve TFMs: spending more latent compute at inference on hard or ambiguous cases could help them make better use of the in-context examples. Almost all existing work on latent reasoning targets natural language, and its transfer to tabular models, whose architecture, pre-training data and output differ profoundly, remains largely unexplored. 

Mechanistic interpretability is starting to open the black box, both for latent-reasoning language models and for TFMs themselves [4]. It lets us ask not only whether latent reasoning improves a TFM, but also what the model actually computes during these extra steps, and whether that computation is faithful and useful. The internship therefore has two goals: designing and evaluating latent reasoning mechanisms for TFMs, and using interpretability methods to analyze what they learn. 

The intern will work with senior researchers and data scientists. This internship offers an opportunity to contribute to an emerging research topic at the intersection of tabular modeling, latent reasoning and interpretability. 

Key Responsibilities 

The intern will: 

  • Review the literature on latent reasoning (NLP) and tabular foundation models, building on recent surveys. 

  • Identify and adapt latent reasoning mechanisms to TFM architectures (e.g. iterative depth-wise computation, hidden-state reuse). 

  • Implement them on open-source TFMs and measure their effect on accuracy, calibration and robustness against strong baselines (gradient boosting, standard TFMs) at comparable compute. 

  • Apply interpretability methods (representation analysis, probing, activation patching) to characterize the computation performed during latent reasoning. 

  • Build an evaluation protocol on diverse tabular datasets, including realistic business cases. 

  • Document the results and contribute to scientific publications. 

Profile 

  • Currently in the final year of a Master’s or Engineering degree, with strong foundations in machine learning, statistics, and programming. 

  • Good grasp of model validation: train/test splits, data leakage, baselines. 

  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to work autonomously on an open-ended research problem. 

  • Knowledge of transformers and language models; familiarity with latent reasoning or recurrent-depth models is a plus. 

  • Strong Python and PyTorch skills, and a solid command of the standard data science toolkit (pandas/polars, scikit-learn, gradient-boosting libraries). 

  • Fluency in English is a plus. 

  • Nice to have: experience in interpretability, knowledge of TabPFN, TabICL or TabDPT, and solid software engineering practices (git, code review, testing). 

Benefits 

  • Hands-on Research & Engineering Experience: Build a pioneering agentic system on real data science workflows, contributing to a tool with direct real-world impact. 

  • Collaborative Learning: Engage with a team of data scientists, AI experts, and PhDs in a dynamic, research-driven environment within Ekimetrics' Innovation Department. 

  • Skill Development: Gain expertise in LLM agents, the evaluation of AI systems, and production tooling on Databricks (Unity Catalog, MLflow). 

  • Career Growth: Opportunity to transition into a full-time Data Scientist role in AI at Ekimetrics, or into a PhD program, upon successful completion of the internship. 

  • Scientific Contribution: Opportunity to co-author and publish scientific papers in reputable AI and data science conferences and journals. 

  • Networking: Collaborate with Ekimetrics' industrial and academic partners, enhancing your professional network in the AI research community. 

  • Ethical and Sustainable AI: Learn to develop AI solutions that align with ethical, governed, and sustainable best practices, a core commitment of Ekimetrics. 

Duration: 6 months, Paris 

References 

[1] Zhu, R.-J. et al. (2025). A Survey on Latent Reasoning. arXiv:2507.06203. 

[2] Chen, X. et al. (2025). Reasoning Beyond Language: A Comprehensive Survey on Latent Chain-of-Thought Reasoning. arXiv:2505.16782. 

[3] Tabular Foundation Models: A Systematic Survey. [authors, year, link to complete] 

[4] Biloš, M. et al. (2026). A Mechanistic Study of Tabular Foundation Models. [link to complete]

jobs.description:
Help Us Build The Future of Travel

At Airalo, we're making it easier for people to stay connected wherever they travel. As the world's first eSIM store, we help millions of travelers access affordable mobile data in 200+ countries and regions around the world.

Today, we're a team of 400+ people across 60+ countries, building a product used by travelers every day. We've grown quickly, but we've worked hard to keep what matters: trust, ownership, and the freedom for people to do great work without unnecessary layers or bureaucracy.

We're fully remote by design, genuinely global, and united by a shared mission to make travel simpler for everyone.

Your Next Destination

  • Location: Remote.
  • Contract: Full-time, permanent.
  • Benefits: Learn more about our benefits here in this link - https://airalo-public.notion.site/Benefits-25396a97ffca81fb9bc1f0be479f1be3?pvs=74 
  • Languages: English is our main working language day to day, so you'll need to be comfortable communicating in it both in meetings and async.

 


We're looking for a Staff Data Scientist, Pricing to build the analytical and machine learning capability that pricing runs on, from demand modelling through to the systems that recommend price.

You won't be starting from zero. We've invested in the foundational data and infrastructure that pricing decisions depend on. What's missing is the capability on top: models the business trusts, experiments that settle pricing questions with evidence, and economics defined once so they hold consistently across Commercial, Product and the customer experience.

The arc of the role runs from measurement to prediction to prescription - understanding how demand responds to price, forecasting how it will respond, and ultimately building the models that recommend the price itself.


What You'll Do:

  • Build and own the demand and elasticity modelling capability, quantifying how price affects volume across destination, duration, data tier, and customer segment.

  • Develop machine learning models for demand forecasting and willingness-to-pay, and take them from exploration through to production with the monitoring and retraining that keeps them honest.

  • Move us from predictive to prescriptive by building the optimisation layer that turns forecasts and elasticities into recommended prices under margin, competitive and partner constraints.

  • Design and analyse pricing experiments with statistical rigour, and apply causal methods where clean randomisation isn't possible.

  • Define pricing within our data ecosystem, owning the governed definitions of price, cost and package economics that reporting, analysis and product surfaces all read from.

  • Partner with Commercial and Finance to connect pricing decisions to margin and revenue, and to size opportunities before we commit.

  • Set the analytical standard for pricing at Airalo, from what counts as evidence through to how a model or recommendation gets validated before it influences live pricing.


    • What You'll Bring:

  • 7+ years in data science, quantitative economics, or applied research, including pricing, monetisation, or marketplace economics work that demonstrably changed decisions.

  • Experience with dynamic or algorithmic pricing systems in production.

  • An advanced degree in Econometrics, Statistics, Operations Research or similar, or equivalent applied depth in demand estimation and the identification problems that make naive price-quantity regressions wrong.

  • Hands-on machine learning experience across the full lifecycle, from feature engineering and model selection through to deployment

  • Familiarity with optimisation and decision-science methods that turn predictions into recommended actions, whether through constrained optimisation, bandits, or reinforcement learning approaches.

  • Proven experimentation expertise, having designed and defended experiments with a clear view on decision frameworks and common failure modes.

  • Experience building analytical capability where none existed before, turning raw data and a business question into something a commercial team uses repeatedly.

  • Strong data modelling instincts, thinking in reusable definitions and single sources of truth rather than standalone analyses.

  • The ability to move comfortably between financial, product and operational data and connect the analysis to a financial outcome.

  • Genuine partnership instincts, translating between analytical rigour and commercial reality so that Commercial and Product come to you early rather than after the decision.

  • Fluency in the Python ML stack alongside strong SQL, with the engineering hygiene to hand over code that others can run and maintain.

  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to make a methodological argument to people who won't check your standard errors.

  • A self-starter mindset that thrives in ambiguity and brings structure without waiting for permission.

  • Comfort using AI tools to augment analytical work, with a point of view on where they help and where they don't


    • Nice to have:

  • Experience in marketplace, telecom, travel, or subscription/usage-based businesses.

  • Bayesian or hierarchical modelling for sparse segments and long-tail SKUs.

  • Competitive price response modelling, or working with scraped competitor pricing data.

  • Familiarity with dbt, LightDash, or similar semantic/BI layers.

  • Experience designing semantic or metric layers consumed by both analytics and production systems.

  • Experience working in cross-functional teams spanning commercial, finance and product disciplines.

    • If you are interested in this position, please apply via the link.

    Why People Join Us

    We started Airalo to make staying connected effortless, wherever you are in the world. Today, millions of travelers rely on our eSIMs, and many of the people building the product were customers first.

    Our team spans 60+ countries, united by a shared belief that great work happens when people are trusted to own what they do. There's trust to own what you do, space to focus without constant layers of process, and a clear sense of what you're responsible for from day one.

    As Airalo continues to grow, so do the opportunities to learn, take on new challenges, and make a real impact - from anywhere in the world.

We’re looking for a Director, Enterprise IT to build and lead a new function at Airalo. Enterprise IT is responsible for the IT estate our team members use every day and the core business systems that run the company, starting with ERP and expanding to the wider corporate application stack as we scale.

This is a build-and-run role. You’ll lead an established IT Operations team (a lead and a team of four) covering service management, endpoints, networking, identity and SSO. You’ll also be the accountable technical owner of our ERP platform, from implementation into steady state. As more corporate tooling moves into your remit, you’ll recruit and structure an Enterprise Applications team and move us away from every function buying and running its own critical systems. Business functions keep ownership of their processes, data and decisions.

You’ll have real ownership in shaping how systems are configured, governed and supported, and in building the team and operating model that carries us through the next stage of growth.


What you’ll do:
  • Lead the IT Operations team and its lead: set priorities and service levels, with a clear split between run and build work
  • Own service desk performance, request and incident handling, and team member satisfaction
  • Own endpoint and device management, including OS and software update policy, balancing compliance against minimal disruption to people’s work
  • Own identity, SSO, access provisioning and offboarding as a single, auditable control point, and automate joiner, mover and leaver processes and other repeatable IT work
  • Act as the accountable owner of the ERP platform, including system configuration, workflow design and ongoing maintenance. If vendor selection is still open when you join, lead its final stages with stakeholders to confirm scope, modules and implementation approach
  • Own the design of core ERP configuration areas such as financial consolidation, budgeting and forecasting, master data, and integration with adjacent systems
  • Manage the ERP implementation partner or systems integrator, holding them to scope, quality, timeline and budget
  • Establish change control, testing and release processes for ERP from day one, and own the post-go-live support model (L1 to L3, vendor SLAs, release cadence)
  • Document system configuration, data flows and integration points so no single person is a dependency
  • Own IT general controls, segregation of duties design and monitoring, and audit evidence for corporate systems, supporting compliance certification and SOX-style financial controls where they apply
  • Own disaster recovery, backup and resilience for corporate systems, and work with Security on access policy, device trust and approved or blocked software
  • Partner with the Data team: Enterprise IT owns platforms, integrations and access controls, while Data keeps reporting, analytics, pipelines and data governance
  • Set the approach to AI tools across corporate functions (tooling, access and safe-use guardrails), with functions owning day-to-day use
  • Build the Enterprise Applications team: define roles, then hire and develop the first leads (2 to 3 additional hires expected over time)
  • Define the roadmap and Buy / Hold / Sell decisions for bringing additional corporate technology (HR, finance, CRM, collaboration and other SaaS) under Enterprise IT, backed by a lightweight governance model: application inventory, ownership matrix and lifecycle approach
  • Own vendor, licence and SaaS renewal management for in-scope systems, consolidating duplicate tools and spend, along with Enterprise IT’s budget and headcount plan
  • Lead the change from function-owned tools to centrally governed systems without taking process ownership away from the business, and act as a trusted advisor to leadership on application strategy, cost and risk

jobs.description:
Co-Founder | Growth, Community & Partnerships (m/w/d)

Standort: München (überwiegend vor Ort)
Start: Voraussichtlich Februar/März 2027
Compensation: EXIST Gründungsstipendium, 2.500 € monatlich für Hochschulabsolventen, plus geplante Beteiligung am Unternehmen

Über uns

Wir sind Pierre-Louis Suckrow und Kerim Anater. Unsere akademischen und beruflichen Hintergründe liegen in Informatik, Design & Computation und Human Computer Interaction. Gemeinsam entwickeln wir eine neue Plattform für die Organisation und Zusammenarbeit in der digitalen Musikproduktion.

Unser Produkt soll es ermöglichen, verschiedene Projektstände und ihre Entstehung nachzuvollziehen, frühere Versionen wiederherzustellen und Projekte zwischen unterschiedlichen Produktionsumgebungen auszutauschen. Damit möchten wir mehr Raum für musikalisches Experimentieren schaffen, den organisatorischen Aufwand in kreativen Arbeitsprozessen reduzieren und die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Musikschaffenden erleichtern.

Ein erster funktionsfähiger Prototyp für Ableton Live existiert bereits. Wir sind Teil des WaveLab Inkubators Batch #7 und im Wintersemester Teil der Munich Music Labs. Aktuell bereiten wir unsere Bewerbung für das EXIST Gründungsstipendium vor.

Zur Ergänzung unserer technischen und produktorientierten Kompetenzen suchen wir ein drittes Gründungsmitglied, das insbesondere die Kommunikation nach außen, den Aufbau von Kontakten und die Entwicklung von Kundenbeziehungen mitgestaltet.

Deine Rolle

In der kommenden Projektphase stehen die Weiterentwicklung des Produkts, die Validierung mit potenziellen Nutzern und der Aufbau erster Kundenbeziehungen und Partnerschaften im Vordergrund.

Wir suchen eine Person, die diese Prozesse begleitet und insbesondere den Austausch mit Menschen außerhalb unseres Teams übernimmt.

Mögliche Schwerpunkte sind:

  • Communications & PR: Entwicklung unserer Außenkommunikation, Vermittlung unserer Produktidee und Aufbau von Sichtbarkeit innerhalb der Musikbranche und darüber hinaus.

  • Community Building: Aufbau und Betreuung einer Community aus Musikproduzenten, Musikschaffenden und weiteren potenziellen Nutzern.

  • Partnerships & Networking: Kontaktaufnahme und Beziehungspflege mit Studios, Unternehmen, Branchenakteuren und potenziellen Kooperationspartnern.

  • Customer Discovery & Success: Durchführung von Gesprächen mit potenziellen Nutzern, Begleitung erster Beta User und Pilotprojekte sowie systematische Erfassung von Feedback.

  • Growth & Business Development: Mitentwicklung unserer Go to Market Strategie, Erschließung erster Kundengruppen und Validierung unseres Geschäftsmodells.

Die genaue Aufgabenverteilung möchten wir gemeinsam und abhängig von deinen bisherigen Erfahrungen und Interessen entwickeln.

Als drittes Gründungsmitglied bist du darüber hinaus an der strategischen und unternehmerischen Entwicklung des Vorhabens beteiligt.

Wen wir suchen

Wir suchen eine kommunikative und eigenständig arbeitende Person, die gerne mit Menschen in Kontakt tritt und Interesse daran hat, ein technologisches Produkt von der frühen Entwicklung bis zum Markteintritt zu begleiten.

Idealerweise bringst du Folgendes mit:

  • Erfahrung in einem kommunikationsorientierten Bereich, beispielsweise PR, Marketing, Community Management, Customer Success, Sales, Account Management oder Business Development.

  • Die Fähigkeit, komplexe Ideen verständlich zu kommunizieren und unterschiedliche Zielgruppen anzusprechen.

  • Freude am Aufbau und an der Pflege von Kontakten und langfristigen Beziehungen.

  • Eigeninitiative, organisatorische Fähigkeiten und die Bereitschaft, Verantwortung zu übernehmen.

  • Interesse an digitalen Produkten, Technologie und kreativen Arbeitsprozessen.

  • Interesse an der gemeinsamen Gründung und langfristigen Entwicklung eines Unternehmens.

Nice to have, aber keine Voraussetzung:

  • Erfahrung in der Musikindustrie oder Kontakte zu Musikproduzenten, Studios, Labels oder Artists.

  • Erfahrung mit Startups, Software Produkten oder dem Aufbau von Communities.

  • Eigene Erfahrung oder Interesse im Bereich Musikproduktion.

Ein bestimmter beruflicher Hintergrund ist für uns nicht ausschlaggebend. Entscheidend sind die Bereitschaft, sich in neue Themen einzuarbeiten, eigenständig Verantwortung zu übernehmen und die fachliche sowie persönliche Ergänzung innerhalb unseres Gründungsteams.

EXIST Förderung & Compensation

Wir bereiten aktuell unseren Antrag für das EXIST Gründungsstipendium vor. Das Förderprogramm unterstützt Gründungsteams über einen Zeitraum von zwölf Monaten bei der Entwicklung und Validierung ihres Gründungsvorhabens.

Während der Förderung erhält jedes Teammitglied abhängig von der Qualifikation ein monatliches Stipendium:

  • 2.500 € pro Monat mit Hochschulabschluss

  • 3.000 € pro Monat mit Promotion

  • 2.000 € pro Monat mit anerkanntem Berufsabschluss

  • 1.000 € pro Monat als Student oder Studentin

Das Stipendium dient der Sicherung des Lebensunterhalts und ist kein reguläres Angestelltengehalt. Die Förderung steht unter dem Vorbehalt der Bewilligung unseres EXIST Antrags.

Voraussetzungen für die EXIST Förderung:

  • Ein Hochschulabschluss, der in der Regel nicht länger als fünf Jahre zurückliegt, oder eine andere nach EXIST zulässige Qualifikation. Für eine Person im Gründungsteam sind Ausnahmen möglich.

  • Ein Wohnsitz in Deutschland beziehungsweise die Möglichkeit, während der Förderung in Deutschland zu leben und sich hier anzumelden.

  • Die Bereitschaft, sich während der Förderphase in Vollzeit dem Gründungsvorhaben zu widmen.

Weitere Informationen zum Förderprogramm findest du auf der offiziellen EXIST Website.

Wir suchen ausdrücklich ein langfristiges Gründungsmitglied und keine befristete Anstellung. Wir streben eine weitgehend gleichberechtigte Beteiligung am zukünftigen Unternehmen an. Die konkrete Ausgestaltung möchten wir gemeinsam besprechen.

Zusammenarbeit

Wir sind derzeit in München und Berlin ansässig. Für die Gründungsphase möchten wir das Team in München zusammenbringen, um die Produktentwicklung und den Unternehmensaufbau gemeinsam vor Ort voranzutreiben.

Daher suchen wir jemanden, der bereits in München lebt oder bereit ist, für die gemeinsame Gründungsphase nach München zu ziehen.

Da wir uns noch in einer frühen Entwicklungsphase befinden, sind viele Aspekte der späteren Unternehmensstruktur und Aufgabenverteilung noch offen. Diese möchten wir gemeinsam als Gründungsteam gestalten.

Interesse?

Wenn du dir vorstellen kannst, unser Gründungsteam zu ergänzen, freuen wir uns über eine kurze Vorstellung und Informationen zu deinem bisherigen Hintergrund.

Weitere Informationen zum Produkt, unserer bisherigen Forschung und dem geplanten Gründungsvorhaben teilen wir gerne in einem persönlichen Gespräch.

jobs.title: Chief of Staff
jobs.description:
About Nous

Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.

We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money.

We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked.

Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent.

And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".

The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.

 

Why we're hiring

Nous runs on small teams with real ownership and barely any middle management. That's a big part of how about 30 of us became one of the UK's fastest-growing startups. It also means the work of joining everything up has been spread across the founders and leads, squeezed in around their day jobs. Plans, OKRs, closing the hires that matter, the big company pushes: everyone does a bit of it and nobody owns it.

Last week showed what happens when someone does. We ran "crunch week": five days where most of the company dropped its normal work to relaunch Nous as a household agent. Twelve workstreams, one owner each, a short daily sync and a pre-mortem. In a week we rebuilt onboarding and the website, shipped new agent capabilities, and got legal, security and comms ready for launch. As one of the team said afterwards, when we cluster around a problem for a bit, we do loads of work.

We want that pace more of the time, without a founder having to drop everything to run it. So we're hiring a Chief of Staff.

 

About the role

You'll work directly with Greg (our CEO) and the founding team, and own how Nous runs day to day: the pace, planning and OKRs, and the big company pushes, plus overseeing hiring and helping land the hires that matter most. You'll sit in the management meeting and get the full picture, including the things that aren't public yet. And you'll have the authority to change how we work: cancel or reshape meetings, and move people and cut scope during a big push.

You enjoy coordinating, but only because it gets things done faster. You'd rather get a decision made today than design a process for making decisions.

 

What you'll actually do

  • Set the pace. Spot what's stuck, work out why, and get it moving. Usually it's a decision nobody has made yet, so you get it made, or make it yourself.

  • Own planning and OKRs. Quarterly OKRs, the weekly management meeting, planning and offsites. Squads run pretty autonomously; you make sure they're working to the same priorities. Each of these should take up less of everyone's time with you running it, not more.

  • Own the scorecard. Keep the numbers behind our OKRs current, and say each week what's off track and why. You pull the data yourself (SQL, our BI tool, a spreadsheet) rather than chasing people for updates.

  • Run the big pushes. The next crunch week is yours: scope it with the leadership team, pick the owners, run it, and write up what we'd do differently next time.

  • Oversee hiring, and help close the hires that matter. Hiring managers run their own processes, and you won't be running ten of them. But you'll keep an eye on all of them, know where every search stands, and jump in where needed. Mostly that's closing the people we really want: working out what they care about and how to win them. Sometimes it's getting a recruiter excited about working with Nous, or unsticking a process that's gone quiet.

  • Represent Nous. You'll talk to recruiters and senior candidates from day one. Over time, and where it helps, you'll represent us to partners, suppliers and investors too.

  • Automate the boring bits. You'd rather build the Monday status digest with Claude than write it by hand every week. Anything you find yourself doing every week is a candidate for automating.

 

What this role isn't

  • An assistant. Diaries and inboxes are someone else's job.

  • A process role. If your first instinct is a new meeting, template or tracker, this probably won't suit you. With you here we should have fewer recurring meetings, not more.

  • A product role. Squads own what gets built, and strategy stays with the founders. You'll be in the room for both, and you make sure nobody's blocked.

  • A recruiter. You oversee hiring and step in where it matters; hiring managers still run their own processes.

  • A dumping ground for jobs nobody else wants. You'll pick up odd jobs, as everyone here does, but the bulk of the role is above.

 

What success looks like

In your first 90 days:

  • The company runs noticeably better: decisions get made faster and fewer things stall. Ask the leads and they'd say so.

  • Something that had been stuck for weeks has shipped because you got involved.

  • You've helped close at least one hire we really wanted.

  • Next quarter's OKRs are set, and the scorecard is current every week.

  • At least one piece of weekly coordination (the OKR update, the status round-up) runs as an AI workflow you built, and nobody does it by hand any more.

  • We have fewer recurring meetings than when you joined.

After a year:

  • You've led two or three company-wide pushes that shipped what they set out to.

  • The senior hires you helped close have said yes and are doing well.

  • Planning, OKRs and the weekly meetings run fine for a month without you.

  • Most of the routine coordination runs on workflows and tools you built, not on meetings.

 

About you

You've got 4–7 years behind you (perhaps a little more if you've switched careers), probably a mix of a fast-growing startup and somewhere that taught you structure: consulting, BizOps or strategy and ops at a scale-up, a founder's office, or product work where you ran launches across teams. Maybe you've founded something.

You coordinate because you're impatient. You notice the thing that's been stuck for a week, and you're the one who unsticks it.

You're persuasive. You can work out what a candidate is really optimising for and how to close them, get a busy recruiter excited about Nous, and hold your own with senior people outside the company.

You're comfortable with numbers. You can build a quick model, write a bit of SQL or find the right dashboard, and tell a real trend from noise.

AI tooling is already how you work. Claude, Claude Code or similar is where you get things done, not something you tried once.

You write clearly and quickly. Most of this job happens in writing: kick-off notes, weekly updates, closing emails.

You tell people the truth, founders included, and you keep confidences. You'll see salaries, plans and people issues before anyone else does.

You listen and you care, but you don't do politics. This role has more connective tissue with others than anyone else in the business, so by playing it straight and being an honest broker, you are also establishing an important norm.

Low ego. Some of the job is unglamorous and you do it anyway.

Bonus points:

  • You've closed hard candidates, or worked in recruiting, talent or BD.

  • You've run a company planning cycle, an offsite or a launch end to end.

  • You've worked somewhere regulated (energy, fintech, insurance).

  • You've automated a chunk of your own job and have something to show for it.

  • You are commercially astute or professionally experienced in a deep domain like law or accounting.

 

How you will grow

This might not be a forever role, and that's fine. You'll see more of how a fast-growing company works than almost anyone else here, which tends to open doors: running a new category as we expand, leading a function, or a commercial or operations role. Or the role grows with the company. Either way, we'll talk about it properly once you've been here a year.

 

Remuneration and benefits

Compelling packages, including share options with life-changing upside. We've raised enough money to pay real salaries. We're building something great together and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together.

An environment where you can do your best work:

  • 🏢 A great office set up for lots of collaborative working. We already need more whiteboards

  • 💻 The equipment / setup / training you need to do your best work (and of course, AI subscriptions, including Claude Code Max tier)

  • 🤝 A high-context environment with lots of exposure to the big decisions - be in the room when it happens (literally)

  • 🏡 Flexibility around remote work. If you sometimes just need to get your head down, that's fine

  • ☕ Very good coffee

  • 🍽️ A well-stocked kitchen (featuring a wildly popular toastie maker) so you can always make yourself a breakfast or light lunch on the house

  • 🎉 Informal social every week, something bigger every month, plus a set-piece event in the summer and again at Christmas - we're not robots!

  • ✈ 33 days paid holidays (including bank holidays)

  • 💊 Health and dental cash plans, including an employee assistance programme

  • 🚴 Travel benefits, including the cycle-to-work scheme and season ticket loans

Nous has an office-first culture. That means we encourage in-person working, and most people do work from the office in Farringdon most of the time. We do a lot of brainstorming, problem-solving and interaction within the team and presence makes this more effective. It also helps ensure people have good peripheral awareness and high context. But we are pragmatic not doctrinal about this, and recognise that, sometimes, certain types of work can be better done remotely. Most team members spend 3-4 days a week in the office on average. This role may naturally involve even more presence than that.

 

The environment

Most importantly, this is a high-performance, high-agency and high-trust technical environment. Nous is intentionally lean and AI-native, not just in its product but as a company. Everyone is expected to use AI to its full potential, whether that's debugging a system, streamlining a workflow or improving how customers are served. Rather than building layers of middle management, we hire smart, high-agency people and give them real ownership.

We're dedicated to fostering an inclusive and equitable workplace, and we actively welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds. Every candidate is thoughtfully considered, without regard to race, religion, gender expression, disability or sexual orientation.

If you don't tick every box but think you'd be great at this, get in touch anyway.
